title: 对称提升的逐层相容实现

preserved: A finite group G and an arbitrary field k, with no invertibility condition on |G|.
Finite-dimensional linear representations, exact rows and equivariant structural maps.
removed: A single short exact sequence with a specified merely k-linear splitting.
added: A countable inverse tower of exact rows with one fixed finite-dimensional quotient representation C and identity transition on C.
Each row admits an equivariant linear section; no compatible family is supplied.
Equivariant transition maps on A_n and B_n commute with each row; no surjectivity assumption.
changed_assumptions.reason: Local equivariant existence is now real input, so the task measures coherent assembly rather than one elementary linear obstruction quotient. Fixed C makes composition with beta_n a genuine map of section spaces.

removed: An explicitly requested choice-independent obstruction and its vanishing criterion for one row.
added: Construct an infinite coherent family of equivariant sections.
Construct an equivariant limit direct-sum decomposition respecting inclusion and projection.
Classify all coherent sections and their transport through isomorphisms of the whole tower.
preserved: Precise freedom of solutions and equivariant diagram-isomorphism transport.
changed_goal.reason: This replaces actual input data and the final mathematical goal. It is not a cosmetic removal of the word obstruction or a relabeling of the old H1 calculation.

necessary_main_goal_specs: The field remains arbitrary; each finite-dimensional row actually has an equivariant section.
The fixed quotient C and exact transition identities are required to make the coherence equations well defined.
The countable index, exact formulas for A_infinity/B_infinity and the required inclusion/projection identities specify the output.
The task requests some coherent family and transport of the entire solution space, not a natural preferred family.
advance_solution_hints_removed: Vanishing as a preannounced necessary-and-sufficient answer.
Averaging, stable-image, Mittag-Leffler or compactness instructions.
precise_minimal_completion_criterion: Prove existence of a coherent equivariant section family for every input tower; use it to give the specified limit decomposition; characterize all such families and verify the stated isomorphism transport. A valid short application of a fully applicable affine inverse-limit or linear-solvability theorem completes the task. No author-specific sequence of lemmas, counterexamples, effective algorithm or canonical selected point is required.

shortest_valid_route.description: Each row-section set is a nonempty finite-dimensional affine space. Postcomposition yields an affine tower. Its images in each fixed level form a descending chain and stabilize; transition maps between stable images are surjective. Recursively choose a coherent point, assemble the limit splitting, and identify differences with lim Hom_G(C,A_n).
shortest_valid_route.difficulty_caveat: The structural improvement over the old linear-cokernel exercise is proved, but a knowledgeable solver may give a short Mittag-Leffler or linear-compactness argument. This is not evidence of high empirical difficulty or a guaranteed long answer.

temptation_points: Choose independently at every level and treat the result as coherent.
Assume beta_n or section transitions are onto.
Average by the order of G in arbitrary characteristic.
Confuse finite dimension with finite cardinality or compactness.
Use nonemptiness of each level without proving stabilization.
Convert a natural solution-space transport into a natural selected splitting.
Reuse the old modular counterexample even though it violates the new local splitting assumption.
proved_structure_tests: A finite-dimensional tower with beta(a,c)=(0,c) shows transitions need not be surjective.
A characteristic-p unipotent modular example shows that removing the local equivariant-splitting assumption changes the theorem.
The k[t] tower beta(a,c)=(ta+c,c) shows local sections need not have a coherent family after removing finite-dimensionality.
A constant split tower with shear automorphisms shows that a natural preferred section is a separate false strengthening.
